Topic: Binary Logic in the Towers of Hanoi

Target audience: High school students interested in computer science and discrete mathematics

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite: The Binary Language

Lecture lines:
Binary systems use only two digits: zero and one.
Each position represents an increasing power of two.
Four bits can represent numbers from zero to fifteen.
Binary is the language of all modern computers.
[Asset: light_bulbs_animation]

Planned animations:
Display bit string '001' at center; color #FFFFFF.
Flash '001' in #FFD700 to emphasize bit length.
Transform '001' into '010' via smooth motion.

Section: section_2 — The Towers of Hanoi Puzzle

Lecture lines:
The puzzle has three rods and stacked discs.
Move one disc at a time between rods.
Never place a larger disc on a smaller one.
The goal is moving all discs to another rod.
[Asset: hanoi_puzzle_setup]

Planned animations:
Render 3 disks on tower; label 'A', 'B', 'C'.
Highlight largest disk at bottom of tower A.
Animate move of largest disk to tower C.

Section: section_3 — Mapping Moves to Binary Codes

Lecture lines:
We label moves from one to two power n.
Binary digits map directly to disc moves.
The lowest set bit determines which disc moves.
[Asset: binary_mapping_table]

Planned animations:
Display 'Disk 1' next to 'Bit 0'; use #00FFFF.
Display 'Disk 2' next to 'Bit 1'; use #FF00FF.
Connect disks and bits with #808080 lines.

Section: section_4 — The Binary Direction Rule

Lecture lines:
Smallest discs follow a strict cyclic pattern.
Larger discs move based on binary parity rules.
This ensures the puzzle is always solved correctly.
[Asset: robot_disc_path]

Planned animations:
Show rule: '0 = move right', '1 = move left'.
Highlight '0' in #00FF00, '1' in #FF0000.
Animate disk movement following these directions.

Section: section_5 — Summary and Real-world Application

Lecture lines:
The puzzle acts like a simple binary counter.
Binary logic governs complex recursive algorithms.
Counting cycles drive fundamental computer processes.
[Asset: computer_clock_cycle]

Planned animations:
Display summary list of steps covered.
Flash binary code summary in #FFFF00.
Show icon representing disk array application.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
